narrative.overview:
BrainFit Karşıyaka is a cognitive development center, not a hospital and not a generic wellness brand. The visual language must carry both at once: the clinical credibility of a structured 45-minute assessment and the human warmth of a team that genuinely cares about cognitive growth. Every design decision is tested against this double standard. If a choice reads as sterile hospital, it fails. If it reads as soft wellness-retreat, it also fails.

The palette is drawn from BrainFit's PMS brand library (Vivid Orange 1505, Golden Yellow 7548, Rich Magenta 233, Bright Cyan 299, Fresh Green 361, Charcoal Gray 11) adapted to web density. The display font (Fraunces) is the authority voice; the body font (Manrope) is the practical voice. The two personas never reverse.

The adults page runs a second North Star in parallel: 'Growth without overwhelm.' Both pages share the palette family; they do not share hero patterns.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream canvas with a coral brand accent — never cold white or clinical grey
Display serif (Fraunces) for authority, extrabold sans (Manrope) for utility — never mixed within a single content role
Full-radius pill shapes on all interactive elements — buttons, chips, badges, inputs
Soft diffuse warm shadows signal interactivity and containment, not decoration — sections are flat by default
Two-audience architecture: parents (coral, warm-organic) and adults (forest green, purposeful-focused) share colors but have distinct hero personalities

rules.name: The Saturation Adaptation Rule
rules.body: The PMS brand colors (1505, 7548, 233, 299, 361) are always used at adapted-for-web saturation. Never reach for the full PMS value in a digital context. Preserve hue identity, not saturation intensity.

rules.name: The Single Surface Rule
rules.body: Coral, forest green, and amber are accent and context colors, not page-level backgrounds. Coral on components only. Forest green on the adult hero section only. Amber as accent text and CTA within forest green contexts only.

rules.name: The Persona Inversion Rule
rules.body: Fraunces carries authority (headings, display, card numeric values). Manrope carries utility (body, labels, buttons). They do not swap. A Manrope heading or a Fraunces button label is a violation.

rules.name: The Weight Anchor Rule
rules.body: Body Manrope is weight 400 in prose, weight 600-700 in description copy, weight 800 in labels and all interactive copy. The jump from 400 to 800 is the hierarchy signal.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Sections sit flat on canvas. Shadows appear on contained components (cards, buttons in elevated states, the form container). A section wrapper with a shadow is always wrong.

dos: Do use .cta-on-coral (canvas fill, espresso text) for any CTA inside a coral-background element.
Do apply text-wrap: balance to all h1-h3 elements.
Do keep Fraunces strictly at font-weight: 650 for display use.
Do use warm shadow tinting (rgba(22,10,8,…) or rgba(36,29,24,…)) not neutral grey.
Do keep all interactive touch targets at min-height: 44px minimum.
Do preserve the two audience personas: parents (coral) and adults (forest green).
Do test muted-brown (#9b745f) at every font size and weight for 4.5:1 contrast.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on all animated elements.
donts: Don't use sterile hospital aesthetics, cold-white backgrounds, or clinical grey typography stacks.
Don't use childish edtech visual patterns: pastel-only palettes, emoji-adjacent icon sets.
Don't use aggressive sales funnel patterns: countdown timers, urgency badges, fear-based copy.
Don't build sections using repeated identical icon cards (icon + heading + text × 6).
Don't use exaggerated metrics or vague transformation promises.
Don't use generic wellness-coach language: 'transform', 'unlock your potential', 'supercharge', 'optimize'.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text + gradient fill).
Don't use side-stripe border cards (border-left accent as decoration).
Don't break the .v4-* class namespace by applying adult hero styles outside a .v4 parent.
Don't make both pages feel identical — they share a palette family, not a pattern.
